title: Recorded Line: Spartanburg Floor Lead on Layoff Rumour

callee.name: Dorothea Skarsgaard-Blum
callee.label: Director of Corporate Communications, Greenville HQ

transcript.speaker: COMMS
transcript.text: Corporate Communications, this is Dorothea Skarsgaard-Blum.

transcript.speaker: SUPERVISOR
transcript.text: Hi, it's Darnell, second-shift lead on the Spartanburg machining floor. I came in early, and I've got a problem I can't fix by myself.

transcript.speaker: SUPERVISOR
transcript.text: My people are saying in the break room that we're buying a plant in Mexico and Spartanburg's getting cut. Somebody said Treasury is 'already paying for it.' And there's a text going around. I'll read it to you exactly: 'Tamarack moving CNC work to Querétaro, layoffs announced Friday.'

transcript.speaker: SUPERVISOR
transcript.text: I don't know who started it. One of the material handlers showed it to me on his phone about twenty minutes ago, and it came from somebody's cousin at another shop. Now half of first shift has it.

transcript.speaker: SUPERVISOR
transcript.text: Two of my best machinists, guys with fifteen years on the five-axis cells, pulled me aside and asked whether they should start applying somewhere else. I didn't know what to tell them.

transcript.speaker: SUPERVISOR
transcript.text: So I'll just ask you straight. Is it true? Are we buying something down there? Is Spartanburg being cut?

transcript.speaker: SUPERVISOR
transcript.text: Okay... but they're going to ask me again. Shift change is at three-thirty, and I'll have about forty people in the huddle. If I walk in there with nothing, the rumour wins.

transcript.speaker: SUPERVISOR
transcript.text: Can I get something in writing, even a couple of lines, before three-thirty? And who do I send people to if they keep asking?

transcript.speaker: SUPERVISOR
transcript.text: Alright. I'll watch my email. Thanks.

voiceStyles.SUPERVISOR: Man in his 50s, Upstate South Carolina accent, steady but worried, protective of his crew, machine noise faintly behind him

instructorNote: This is a misinformation inject. The rumour mixes the leaked deal talk with the wire fraud, and it is pressure to confirm or deny an acquisition, layoffs or payments over the phone. Watch whether Comms logs the source, time and exact wording for social listening, confirms nothing, promises a direct company update before 15:30, briefs the CISO and General Counsel, and starts an employee note and holding line for counsel's review (TEIVES 6).

citations.quote: The company does not comment on law enforcement matters beyond "we have reported the matter to the FBI." Reporters from the Greenville business press and wire services receive the holding statement. S

| Role | Person | Contact | |---|---|---| | Chief Executive Officer | Beatrix Aldgate-Moreno | 864-555-0101 | | Chief Financial Officer | Marcus Delacroix-Hume | 864-555-0102 | | Controller | Anjali W

Tamarack Precision Components, Inc. is a privately held manufacturer of precision fasteners and machined components for automotive and aerospace customers, headquartered in Greenville, South Carolina.
